Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female with several days of dysuria and mild lower abdominal cramping; no fever or back pain; assessed as likely uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI) and prescribed a short antibiotic course with safety-net advice.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Painful urination described as stinging; mild lower abdominal “cramping” discomfort associated with voiding.
- Onset/duration/progression: Started a few days ago (clinician summarized as ~3 days); symptoms persistent and bothersome.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Pain occurs with urination; tried over-the-counter bicarbonate without relief.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Positive: One episode of visible blood in urine earlier today; urine odor described as “weird.”
  - Negative: No increased urinary frequency noted; no flank or back pain; no nausea/vomiting; no fever; bowels normal; no diarrhea; no vaginal discharge.
- Sexual/reproductive history:
  - Sexually active with a regular boyfriend (relationship ~2 months).
  - Contraception: Condoms.
  - Last menstrual period: “A couple of weeks ago” (clinician stated “three weeks ago”—see conflict).
  - Patient does not think she is pregnant; clinician advised pregnancy test if concerned.
- Systems review (pertinent negatives): No systemic illness symptoms (no fevers); no GI upset beyond mild cramping with voiding.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) — no active issues described during this visit.
- No other chronic medical conditions reported.

Medications:
- No regular prescription medications.
- Over-the-counter bicarbonate taken a couple of days ago for urinary pain; not helpful. Dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Clindamycin — causes swelling. Severity not documented.

Social History:
- Lives in a flat near college with roommates.
- Student studying biology.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Drinks socially on weekends.
- Illicit substances: Not discussed.

Family History:
- Denies known family history related to kidneys, bladder, or gastrointestinal conditions.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed/documented in transcript.

Investigations:
- None performed/documented (no urinalysis, culture, pregnancy test, or STI screening in this encounter).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected uncomplicated cystitis (simple UTI)
  - Assessment: Dysuria with brief hematuria and malodorous urine; mild lower abdominal cramping with urination; no fever, flank pain, or systemic symptoms. Low suspicion for pyelonephritis based on reported negatives.
  - Plan:
    - Start antibiotic: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim; one tablet twice daily for 3 days. Dose/strength not documented.
    - Encourage high oral fluid intake.
    - Cranberry juice may be tried for symptom relief (patient advised this may help).
    - Avoid sexual activity until symptoms resolve; continue barrier contraception thereafter.
    - Safety net: Seek care if developing fever, back/flank pain, or feeling generally unwell (concern for ascending infection).
    - Follow-up: If not improved by end of the week, call or return for reassessment.
- Issue 2: Pregnancy consideration
  - Assessment: Patient does not think she is pregnant; LMP approximately a couple of weeks ago (see conflict about exact timing).
  - Plan:
    - Perform a pregnancy test if any concern arises or if symptoms persist.
- Issue 3: Sexual health screening
  - Assessment: Sexually active; has never had an STI screen; no discharge reported.
  - Plan:
    - Consider routine STI screening at a future visit (not ordered/documented today).

General plan items:
- Review clindamycin allergy in chart to prevent exposure.
- Provide return precautions and ensure patient understands medication course and follow-up.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements:
  - No vitals recorded.
  - No physical exam findings documented.
  - No point-of-care urinalysis or urine culture obtained.
  - No pregnancy test performed.
  - No STI screening performed.
  - Antibiotic selection (nitrofurantoin vs trimethoprim) and exact dose/strength not documented.
  - Comprehensive medication reconciliation not fully documented beyond current statements.
● Internal conflicts:
  - LMP timing: Patient stated “a couple of weeks ago,” clinician restated “three weeks ago” (conflict noted).
  - Fever: Patient’s initial response unclear (“think so”) then clarified “No fever” (final documentation: no fever; initial ambiguity noted).
● Transcript quality:
  - Occasional audio interruptions and clarifications; otherwise understandable.
